title: حِكَايَةُ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 858–859 (Night 196, continuing nights-195), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 196 continues the tale of Qamar al-Zamān. The vizier who has pulled Marzawān from the sea warns him that, having been the cause of his rescue, he must not become the cause of both their deaths: he is about to pass through a court of emirs and viziers sitting silent on account of Qamar al-Zamān, the sultan’s son. At the name Marzawān knows the youth whose story he has heard from land to land and has come to seek, but he feigns ignorance and asks who he is. The vizier tells him that the prince lies sick on his bed, neither eating, drinking nor sleeping, at death’s door; that three years ago he refused his father’s wish that he marry and was shut up, and in the morning claimed he had seen at his side a girl of indescribable beauty and had exchanged rings with her; and he begs Marzawān not to look at the king’s son but go about his business, for the sultan’s heart is full of rage against him. Marzawān says to himself that this is the one he seeks, follows the vizier up into the palace, and walks straight to Qamar al-Zamān and stands gazing at him, while the vizier, sitting at the prince’s feet, nearly dies of fright and signals to him to leave. Marzawān pretends not to notice, makes certain that this is the man he is looking for — and dawn overtakes Shahrazād. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu wa-al-tisʿūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the sixth and the ninety after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and ninety-sixth night,
sentences.n: al-sādisa, “the sixth”, feminine to agree with layla; then wa-al-tisʿūna, “and the ninety”, and baʿda al-miʾa, “after the hundred”, as in the nights before. The ئ of المائة is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ لَمَّا فَعَلَ مَعَ مَرْزَوَانَ مَا فَعَلَ قَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنِّي كُنْتُ سَبَبًا لِنَجَاتِكَ مِنَ الْغَرَقِ فَلَا تَكُنْ أَنْتَ سَبَبًا لِمَوْتِي وَمَوْتِكَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-wazīra lammā faʿala maʿa Marzawāna mā faʿala qāla lahu iʿlam annī kuntu sababan li-najātika mina al-gharaqi fa-lā takun anta sababan li-mawtī wa-mawtika
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O fortunate king, that the-vizier, when he-did with Marzawān what he-did, said to-him: Know that-I was a-cause for-your-rescue from the-drowning, so-not be you a-cause for-my-death and-your-death.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the vizier had done for Marzawān all that he did, he said to him, “Know that I was the cause of your rescue from drowning; so see that you are not the cause of my death and yours.”
sentences.n: Shahrazād opens the night by repeating the vizier’s last words from the night before. The print again sets السعيدان solid, al-saʿīdu and anna run together; the spacing is kept. faʿala maʿa … mā faʿala, “did with … what he did”: the open relative mā gathers up the rescue, the fresh clothes and the turban without telling them again, and maʿa marks the one the deeds were done for. sababan li-, “a cause of”: li- marks what is caused. lā takun, lā of prohibition with the jussive, “do not be”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مَرْزَوَانُ وَكَيْفَ ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Marzawānu wa-kayfa dhālika
sentences.l: So-said Marzawān: And-how (is) that?
sentences.i: Marzawān said, “And how is that?”
sentences.n: wa-, “and”, at the head of a question ties it to what was just said, as often in speech.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْوَزِيرُ لِأَنَّكَ فِي هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةِ تَطْلُعُ وَتَشُقُّ بَيْنَ أُمَرَاءَ وَوُزَرَاءَ وَالْكُلُّ سَاكِتُونَ لَايَتَكَلَّمُونَ لِأَجْلِ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ ابْنِ السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: qāla al-wazīru li-annaka fī hādhihi al-sāʿati taṭluʿu wa-tashuqqu bayna umarāʾa wa-wuzarāʾa wa-al-kullu sākitūna lā yatakallamūna li-ajli Qamari al-Zamāni ibni al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: Said the-vizier: Because-you in this the-hour (will) go-up and-cleave (your way) between emirs and-viziers, and-the-all (are) silent, not-speaking, for-the-sake (of) Qamar al-Zamān, son (of) the-sultan.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “Because within the hour you will go up and make your way among emirs and viziers, every one of them silent, not a word spoken, on account of Qamar al-Zamān, the sultan’s son.”
sentences.n: li-annaka, “because you”: li- gives the reason. fī hādhihi al-sāʿa, “in this hour”, that is, presently. ṭalaʿa, “to go up”, here up into the palace from the sea; the imperfect looks ahead. shaqqa bayna, “to split (a way) between”, to pass through a crowd. umarāʾ and wuzarāʾ, plurals of amīr and wazīr, are diptotes, so their genitive after bayna ends in -a. wa-al-kullu sākitūna, “and all are silent”, is a circumstantial clause: the court sits mute on the prince’s account. The print runs lā into its verb, لايتكلمون; the spacing is kept. The shadda of لانّك and of وتشقّ is printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ مَرْزَوَانُ ذِكْرَ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ عَرَفَهُ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَسْمَعُ بِحَدِيثِهِ فِى الْبِلَادِ وَأَتَى فِي طَلَبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Marzawānu dhikra Qamari al-Zamāni ʿarafahu li-annahu kāna yasmaʿu bi-ḥadīthihi fī al-bilādi wa-atā fī ṭalabihi
sentences.l: So-when heard Marzawān (the) mention (of) Qamar al-Zamān, he-knew-him, because-he was hearing of-his-story in the-lands, and-had-come in seeking-him.
sentences.i: When Marzawān heard Qamar al-Zamān named, he knew who he was, for he had been hearing his story told throughout the lands, and had come in search of him.
sentences.n: samiʿa bi-, “to hear of”: bi- marks what one hears about. kāna yasmaʿu, kāna with the imperfect, “he had been hearing”, of something that went on over time. fī ṭalabihi, “in quest of him”: ṭalab, “seeking”, is a verbal noun, and the suffix is the one sought. In one line the print writes fī first as فى, with ى, then as في; both are kept. The kasra of ذِكر is printed.

sentences.t: وَلٰكِنَّهُ تَجَاهَلَ وَقَالَ لِلْوَزِيرِ وَمَنْ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākinnahu tajāhala wa-qāla li-al-wazīri wa-man Qamaru al-Zamāni
sentences.l: But-he feigned-ignorance and-said to-the-vizier: And-who (is) Qamar al-Zamān?
sentences.i: But he pretended not to know, and said to the vizier, “And who is Qamar al-Zamān?”
sentences.n: tajāhala, Form VI of jahila, “to feign ignorance”: Form VI often means putting on a state one is not in; compare yataghāfalu at the end of the night, “he pretends not to notice”. The fatḥa of ومَن is printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ هُوَ ابْنُ السُّلْطَانِ شَهْرَمَانَ وَهُوَ ضَعِيفٌ مُلْقًى عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ لَيْسَ لَهُ قَرَارٌ وَلَا يَأْكُلُ وَلَا يَشْرَبُ وَلَا يَنَامُ لَا بِاللَّيْلِ وَلَا بِالنَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru huwa ibnu al-sulṭāni Shahramāna wa-huwa ḍaʿīfun mulqan ʿalā al-firāshi laysa lahu qarārun wa-lā yaʾkulu wa-lā yashrabu wa-lā yanāmu lā bi-al-layli wa-lā bi-al-nahāri
sentences.l: So-said the-vizier: He (is the) son (of) the-sultan Shahramān, and-he (is) sick, cast-down on the-bed; not-is for-him rest, and-not he-eats and-not he-drinks and-not he-sleeps, neither by-the-night nor by-the-day.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “He is the son of Sultan Shahramān. He lies sick, cast down upon his bed, with no rest; he neither eats nor drinks nor sleeps, by night or by day.
sentences.n: ḍaʿīf, “weak”, is the everyday word for “ill” in this Arabic. mulqan, “thrown down”, passive participle of alqā; the edition spells it ملقى, and the tanwīn sits on the qāf. laysa lahu qarārun, “there is not for him a settling”: li- marks the one who has, or here lacks, a thing; qarār is the rest of one who can settle in one place. lā … wa-lā, “neither … nor”; bi- of time, “by night, by day”. The hamza of يأكل is printed.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَشْرَفَ عَلَى الْمَوْتِ وَيَئِسْنَا مِنْ حَيٰوتِهِ وَأَيْقَنَّا بِوَفَاتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ashrafa ʿalā al-mawti wa-yaʾisnā min ḥayātihi wa-ayqannā bi-wafātihi
sentences.l: And-already he-has-come-to-overlook (the) death, and-we-have-despaired of his-life, and-we-are-certain of-his-passing.
sentences.i: He is at death’s door; we have despaired of his life and are sure that he will die.
sentences.n: ashrafa ʿalā, Form IV, “to look down upon”, and so “to be on the brink of”. yaʾisa min, “to despair of”. ayqana bi-, Form IV, “to be certain of”: the verb chooses bi-. The two halves rhyme, ḥayātihi / wafātihi, “his life / his passing”. ḥayāh is printed حيٰوته, with a dagger alif and a wāw, the old Qurʾānic spelling of حياة; it is kept. The hamza of ويئسنا and the shadda of وايقنّا are printed.

sentences.t: وَإِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُطِيلَ النَّظَرَ إِلَيْهِ أَوْ تَنْظُرَ إِلَى غَيْرِ الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي تَحُطُّ فِيهِ رِجْلَكَ وَإِلَّافَتَرُوحُ رُوحُكَ وَرُوحِي
sentences.tr: wa-iyyāka an tuṭīla al-naẓara ilayhi aw tanẓura ilā ghayri al-mawḍiʿi alladhī taḥuṭṭu fīhi rijlaka wa-illā fa-tarūḥu rūḥuka wa-rūḥī
sentences.l: And-beware-you (of) that you-prolong the-gaze at-him, or you-look to other (than) the-place which you-set-down in-it your-foot; and-if-not, then-goes your-soul and-my-soul.
sentences.i: Take care not to let your gaze rest on him, nor look anywhere but the place where you set your foot; otherwise your life is forfeit, and mine.”
sentences.n: iyyāka an, “beware of (doing)”: iyyā- carries the pronoun as the object of an unspoken verb of warning. Look only where you step: ḥaṭṭa rijlahu, “to set down one’s foot”. wa-illā, “and if not”, is in plus lā; the print sets والّافتروح as one word, and the spacing is kept. fa-tarūḥu rūḥuka, “your soul goes”, plays on rāḥa, “to go”, and rūḥ, “soul”. The shadda of تحطّ, and of illā in والّافتروح, is printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ بِاللّٰهِ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ أَرْجُو مِنْ تَفَضُّلَاتِكَ أَنْ تُخْبِرَنِي عَنْ هٰذَا الشَّابِّ الَّذِي وَصَفْتَهُ لِي مَا سَبَبُ هٰذَا الْأَمْرِ الَّذِي هُوَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu bi-Allāhi ʿalayka ayyuhā al-wazīru arjū min tafaḍḍulātika an tukhbiranī ʿan hādhā al-shābbi alladhī waṣaftahu lī mā sababu hādhā al-amri alladhī huwa fīhi
sentences.l: So-he-said to-him: By-God upon-you, O vizier, I-hope from your-kindnesses that you-tell-me about this the-young-man whom you-described-him to-me: what (is the) cause (of) this the-matter which he (is) in-it?
sentences.i: Marzawān said to him, “I adjure you by God, O vizier, and I hope of your kindness that you will tell me about this young man you have described to me: what is the cause of this state he is in?”
sentences.n: bi-Allāhi ʿalayka, “by God upon you”: bi- of the oath, and ʿalā lays the oath on the one addressed. min tafaḍḍulātika, “of your kindnesses”, a courteous plural; rajā min, “to hope of (someone)”. The print sets a fatḥa on the fāʾ, وصفَته, which would read waṣafathu, “she described him”; the mark is misplaced, and the word is pointed here for the sense, waṣaftahu, “you described him”, with the fāʾ unvowelled. The -hu of waṣaftahu and of fīhi are the pronouns that refer back in an Arabic relative clause: “whom you described (him)”, “which he is in (it)”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ لَا أَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَبَبًا إِلَّا أَنَّ وَالِدَهُ مِنْ مُنْذُ ثَلٰثِ سِنِينَ سَأَلَهُ أَنْ يَتَزَوَّجَ فَأَبَي فَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ وَسَجَنَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru lā aʿlamu lahu sababan illā anna wālidahu min mundhu thalāthi sinīna saʾalahu an yatazawwaja fa-abā fa-ghaḍiba ʿalayhi wa-sajanahu
sentences.l: So-said to-him the-vizier: Not I-know for-it a-cause, except that his-father, from since three years, asked-him that he-marry, and-he-refused; so-he-grew-angry with-him and-imprisoned-him.
sentences.i: The vizier answered, “I know of no cause for it, except that three years ago his father asked him to marry and he refused, and his father grew angry with him and shut him up.
sentences.n: min mundhu, “from since”, puts two words for “since” side by side, a spoken habit the edition keeps. thalāth, “three”, is printed ثلٰث with its dagger alif. The print spells abā, “he refused”, with a dotted ي, فابي; it is kept. ghaḍiba ʿalā, “to be angry with”: ʿalā marks the one the anger falls on. The shadda of الّا and the hamza of سأله are printed.

sentences.t: فَأَصْبَحَ وَهُوَ يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ نَائِمًا فَرَأَى بِجَنْبِهِ صَبِيَّةً بَارِعَةَ الْجَمَالِ يَعْجِزُ عَنْ وَصْفِ حُسْنِهَا اللِّسَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-aṣbaḥa wa-huwa yazʿumu annahu kāna nāʾiman fa-raʾā bi-janbihi ṣabiyyatan bāriʿata al-jamāli yaʿjizu ʿan waṣfi ḥusnihā al-lisānu
sentences.l: Then-he-came-to-morning, and-he claiming that-he was sleeping and-saw at-his-side a-girl surpassing (in) the-beauty, (there) falls-short from (the) describing (of) her-loveliness the-tongue.
sentences.i: In the morning he declared that he had been asleep and had seen beside him a girl of surpassing beauty, whose loveliness no tongue could tell.
sentences.n: aṣbaḥa, “to come into the morning”; wa-huwa yazʿumu, “and he claiming”, a circumstantial clause. zaʿama, “to assert”, is often used of a claim the speaker doubts. bāriʿat al-jamāl, “surpassing in beauty”: an adjective in construct with the noun that says in what she excels. ʿajaza ʿan, “to fall short of”; its subject, al-lisānu, “the tongue”, comes last. The hamza of فرأى, the ئ of نائما and the shadda of صبيّة are printed.

sentences.t: وَذَكَرَ لَنَا أَنَّهُ نَزَعَ خَاتَمَهَا مِنْ إِصْبَعِهَا وَلَبِسَهُ وَأَلْبَسَهَا خَاتَمَهُ وَنَحْنُ لَا نَعْرِفُ بَاطِنَ هٰذِهِ الْقَضِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-dhakara lanā annahu nazaʿa khātamahā min iṣbaʿihā wa-labisahu wa-albasahā khātamahu wa-naḥnu lā naʿrifu bāṭina hādhihi al-qaḍiyyati
sentences.l: And-he-told to-us that-he drew-off her-ring from her-finger and-put-it-on, and-put-on-her his-ring; and-we, not we-know (the) inside (of) this the-affair.
sentences.i: He told us that he had drawn her ring from her finger and put it on, and put his own ring on her; and we do not know the truth of this affair.
sentences.n: labisa, “to put on (oneself)”; albasa, Form IV, “to put (something) on (someone)”, takes two objects, here -hā, “her”, and khātamahu, “his ring”. bāṭin, “the inside”, the hidden truth of a thing, as against its ẓāhir, its outward face.

sentences.t: فَبِاللّٰهِ يَا وَلَدِي إِذَا طَلَعْتَ مَعِي إِلَى الْقَصْرِ لَا تَنْظُرْ إِلَى ابْنِ الْمَلِكِ وَرُحْ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ فَإِنَّ السُّلْطَانَ قَلْبُهُ مَلْآنُ عَلَيَّ غَيْظًا
sentences.tr: fa-bi-Allāhi yā waladī idhā ṭalaʿta maʿī ilā al-qaṣri lā tanẓur ilā ibni al-maliki wa-ruḥ ilā ḥāli sabīlika fa-inna al-sulṭāna qalbuhu malʾānu ʿalayya ghayẓan
sentences.l: So-by-God, O my-son, when you-go-up with-me to the-palace, not look at (the) son (of) the-king, and-go to (the) state (of) your-way; for indeed the-sultan, his-heart (is) full against-me (in) rage.
sentences.i: So by God, my son, when you go up with me to the palace, do not look at the king’s son, but go about your business; for the sultan’s heart is full of rage against me.”
sentences.n: bi-Allāhi, bi- of the oath, here pleading. After idhā, Classical Arabic would put fa- before a prohibition (fa-lā tanẓur); the text goes straight on, as speech does. ruḥ ilā ḥāli sabīlika, “go to the state of your way”, that is, about your own affairs. al-sulṭāna qalbuhu malʾānu, “the sultan, his heart is full”: the topic comes first, then a clause about it. ghayẓan, “in rage”, is an accusative of specification after malʾān, “full”; ʿalayya, “against me”. The madda of ملآن and the shadda of عليّ are printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مَرْزَوَانُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَاللّٰهِ إِنَّ هٰذَا هُوَ الْمَطْلُوبُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Marzawānu fī nafsihi wa-Allāhi inna hādhā huwa al-maṭlūbu
sentences.l: So-said Marzawān in himself: By-God, indeed this, he (is) the-sought.
sentences.i: Marzawān said to himself, “By God, this is the very one I seek.”
sentences.n: The print has نقال, a misprint for فقال, corrected here. fī nafsihi, “in his soul”, to himself. wa-Allāhi, wa- of the oath. hādhā huwa al-maṭlūbu: the pronoun huwa sets off the predicate, “this, he is the one sought”; maṭlūb, passive participle of ṭalaba, “to seek”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَلَعَ مَرْزَوَانُ خَلْفَ الْوَزِيرِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭalaʿa Marzawānu khalfa al-wazīri ilā an waṣala ilā al-qaṣri
sentences.l: Then went-up Marzawān behind the-vizier until that he-arrived at the-palace.
sentences.i: Then Marzawān went up behind the vizier until he reached the palace.
sentences.n: ilā an, “until”, literally “to (the point) that”.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَ الْوَزِيرُ تَحْتَ رِجْلَيْ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-jalasa al-wazīru taḥta rijlay Qamari al-Zamāni
sentences.l: And-sat the-vizier beneath (the) two-feet (of) Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.i: The vizier sat down at the feet of Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.n: rijlay, dual of rijl, “foot”, in construct: the dual’s nūn drops before the following genitive. The vizier takes his old place at the foot of the bed.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَرْزَوَانُ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ دَأْبٌ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ مَشَى حَتَّى وَقَفَ قُدَّامَ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ وَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā Marzawānu fa-innahu lam yakun lahu daʾbun illā annahu mashā ḥattā waqafa quddāma Qamari al-Zamāni wa-naẓara ilayhi
sentences.l: And-as-for Marzawān, then-indeed-he, not was for-him a-concern except that-he walked until he-stood before Qamar al-Zamān and-looked at-him.
sentences.i: As for Marzawān, he had no thought but to walk straight on until he stood before Qamar al-Zamān and looked at him.
sentences.n: ammā … fa-, “as for … then”: the fa- is required after ammā. daʾb, “habit, constant business”: lam yakun lahu daʾbun illā, “he had no business but”, that is, he did nothing but this. The hamza of دأب is printed; here illā is printed without its shadda, الا.

sentences.t: فَمَاتَ الْوَزِيرُ فِي جِلْدِهِ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ وَصَارَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى مَرْزَوَانَ وَيَغْمِزُهُ لِيَرُوحَ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهِ وَمَرْزَوَانُ يَتَغَافَلُ وَيَنْظُرُ إِلَى قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-māta al-wazīru fī jildihi mina al-khawfi wa-ṣāra yanẓuru ilā Marzawāna wa-yaghmizuhu li-yarūḥa ilā ḥāli sabīlihi wa-Marzawānu yataghāfalu wa-yanẓuru ilā Qamari al-Zamāni
sentences.l: And-died the-vizier in his-skin from the-fear, and-he-took-to looking at Marzawān and-signalling-him that-he-go to (the) state (of) his-way, and-Marzawān feigning-heedlessness and-looking at Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.i: The vizier all but died of fright; he kept looking at Marzawān and signing to him to go about his business, while Marzawān pretended not to notice and went on gazing at Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.n: māta fī jildihi, “he died in his skin”, an idiom for being frightened half to death; min, “from”, gives the cause. ṣāra with the imperfect, “he took to (doing)”. ghamaza, “to wink, signal with the eye”. li-yarūḥa: li- of purpose with the subjunctive, “that he should go”. yataghāfalu, Form VI, “to feign heedlessness”, the counterpart of tajāhala earlier in the night; wa-Marzawānu yataghāfalu is a circumstantial clause, “while Marzawān …”.

sentences.t: فَتَحَقَّقَ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّهُ هُوَ الْمَطْلُوبُ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥaqqaqa wa-ʿalima annahu huwa al-maṭlūbu
sentences.l: And-he-made-sure and-knew that-he, he (is) the-sought.
sentences.i: And he made certain, and knew that this was the one he sought.
sentences.n: taḥaqqaqa, Form V, “to make sure”; the subject is Marzawān. annahu huwa al-maṭlūbu takes up his oath of a moment before, now as knowledge.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahrazād, and-she-fell-silent from the-permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech allowed her.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as at the end of every night; this time the print sets the name as one word, شهرزاد.
